provenance: New source translation, with E3670-E3679 and E3760-E3769 reviewed.
context: Lady Marbas explains the seal; Gate Keeper and Key Master interrupt. Party receives the Last Psalm, then explores speaking boxes tied to tree names.
decisions: Names follow glossary. Riddle's hope, weight and stone clues preserved literally. Cross-row clauses retain boundaries. Corpse Tree and Last Psalm use provisional descriptive names.

translations.en: protect the seal to the end.
A deal with a monster was unlikely to cost only money or goods.
Especially when the archmage @7rChu Lu Gah@0r had apparently
made a deal with this very monster.
You steeled yourself and declared that you would not make a deal.
That little kitten over there might have agreed.
You pass. Never bargain lightly with a monster.
Especially when you don't know how powerful they are.
Were you planning to ambush me?
No. At most, I'd have sent you home with a painful lesson.
But I won't need to do that now.
To begin with, this is a strange town built
on the legacy of an ancient civilization.
The ruins themselves were sealing something away.
But when @7rChu Lu Gah@0r investigated those ruins,
he realized the seal was beginning to fail.
At the very least, the human world would be destroyed.
Once @7rChu Lu Gah@0r learned that, he began searching
for a spell to reinforce it, even bargaining with monsters.
And that's why you helped him?
I happen to like this world.
That's all the reason I needed to help @7rChu Lu Gah@0r.
I don't know the details of the final seal.
But I do know at least a little about the seal
that's coming undone now.
The recent disturbance freed two monsters.
They're called @7rGate Keeper@0r and @7rKey Master@0r.
@7rGate Keeper@0r and @7rKey Master@0r...
If they reach the sealed gate and work their mischief,
@7rChu Lu Gah's@0r seal on the ruins will be broken.
That would leave only the ruins' own seal
standing in their way.
That's quite enough talk!
I am the fiend of the gate, @7rGate Keeper@0r.
Hee hee hee hee!
And I am the demon of the key, @7rKey Master@0r.
Key Master
A talkative monster and meddling adventurers.
What an unpleasant combination. Hee hee hee hee.
Gate Keeper
We won't let you interfere.
This is where it ends for you.
Corpse Tree! Hang them from your branches!
@7rGate Keeper@0r and @7rKey Master@0r have vanished somewhere.
They've already made it this far...
I suppose it's only a matter of time before they break the seal.
You'll have to stop them before they can do anything.
If you mean to protect this town, see it through to the end.
This is the last clue @7rChu Lu Gah@0r left with me.
Take it with you.
You received the @3rLast Psalm@0r from @7rLady Marbas@0r.
Come again if you need anything else.
Or perhaps I shall summon you myself.
Until then, farewell.
@7rLady Marbas@0r turned to smoke and vanished.
But the @3rLast Psalm@0r remained in your hands.
It proved that @7rLady Marbas@0r had been no dream.
We can't stand around somewhere enemies could appear at any moment
reading the @3rPsalm@0r.
Let's withdraw and analyze it at the tavern!
Following @7rCarmine's@0r advice, you decided to withdraw.
At your feet was a tile depicting a coconut tree.
A small box and a stone statue stood directly before it.
Is this... Cocosnoot?
At the word Cocosnoot, the box began to speak.
Box
Hope is said to be the greatest sin. Still, people seek hope.
Thus hope is weighted down and hidden in a box.
What betrays its hiding place?
Cocosnoot
Amandel
Walnoot
Stone
Hope does not eat nuts.
The moment the box declared that, the statue beside it began moving.
The stone gives hope away without being asked.
Thus the stone was made unable to speak.
After saying this, the box opened with a heavy creak.
Inside were a @3rRed Rod@0r and the words "Hope comes out last,"
written on a message.
